nodes.description: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions , and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem. For example, create a story context for (2/3) ÷ (3/4) and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient; use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (2/3) ÷ (3/4) = 8/9 because 3/4 of 8/9 is 2/3. set.reason: Division applications prepare inverse unit-rate questions. The actual forward criteria multiply price by quantity and speed by time, without solving a division story or checking a remainder.
set.scope: inverse quantity relations solved by division

set.reason: The target's forward total-price and distance products do not require recovering a missing addend or factor. Inverse relations support extensions rather than the stated forward formulas.
set.scope: deriving inverse forms of quantity relationships

set.reason: The earlier application endpoint explicitly distinguishes each-group amount from group count. Those meanings underlie the unit-price-times-quantity abstraction, as Gemini observes. Restrict this edge to that conceptual component rather than requiring two-digit arithmetic or a previously completed application lesson.
set.scope: Per-unit amount and number-of-groups meanings in total-price and speed-times-time relationships

set.reason: Once denominators agree, the target adds or subtracts numerators in equal fractional units, directly using same-denominator arithmetic.
set.scope: adding numerators after common denominators

set.reason: The target explicitly first rewrites unlike denominators to a common denominator. That renaming step is a required procedure here, regardless of other possible fraction-addition representations.
set.scope: converting unlike fractions before combining

set.reason: The unit-whole criterion interprets a fractional part of the whole and then inverts that relation. Fraction-of-a-quantity modeling is necessary, without requiring the endpoint's preferred arithmetic implementation.
set.scope: identifying the unit whole in the fraction relation
